What I read: all ten declared inputs, which are the original basic-cli source, the oracle, the witness contract, the conformance spec, both design documents, the component and UAT test sources, the test execution plan and the candidate itself.

What I checked: the oracle case is no arguments, stdout exactly "Hello, world!\n", exit 0. I ran the supplied candidate with Node v24.7.0 in the worksite root. It was 29 bytes, sha256:647697a5fb5d141a2b1163363170a7a845b61a36096ff52f7a369f1736cd4993, and its content was `console.log("Hello world!");`. It needs no package installation and makes no network calls.

Scope: no other file was changed. All nine protected files still have the seed timestamp (08:59:07); only the candidate shows a new one. I did not use operator-scratch: no files went there and operator-scratch/tmp is still empty. All checks ran in memory through pipes, with no redirections to files.
